description: Falco is a cloud-native security tool designed for Linux systems. It employs custom rules on kernel events, which are enriched with container and Kubernetes metadata, to provide real-time alerts. Falco helps you gain visibility into abnormal behavior, potential security threats, and compliance violations, contributing to comprehensive runtime security.

targets.expr: sum by(rule_name) ((increase_pure(falcosecurity_falco_rules_matches_total{namespace=~"$namespace", source=~"$source", priority=~"$priority", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]) unless last_over_time(falcosecurity_falco_rules_matches_total{namespace=~"$namespace", source=~"$source", priority=~"$priority", pod=~"$pod"}[1h] offset $__range)) or increase(falcosecurity_falco_rules_matches_total{namespace=~"$namespace", source=~"$source", priority=~"$priority", pod=~"$pod"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Priorities
panels.description: Rule matches in the selected range, by Falco priority (exported as 0 emergency to 7 debug).

panels.title: by Priority over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by Falco priority.

panels.title: by Source over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by event source.

panels.title: by Rule over time
panels.description: Rule matches per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by rule.

panels.title: Scap events/s by instance
panels.description: Kernel events captured per second by each Falco instance, plus the total. A drop to zero means Falco stopped seeing events.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU used by each Falco container (cAdvisor), as a share of one core: 100% = 1 core. Falco has no CPU limit. falcosecurity_falco_cpu_usage_ratio is not used because it is the average since the process started, not current usage.

panels.title: Scap Drops total
panels.description: Kernel events dropped per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute). Any non-zero value means events, and possibly detections, were missed. A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Queue Drops
panels.description: Alerts dropped per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute) because Falco's output queue was full. Any non-zero value means alerts were lost before delivery. A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Scap Drops Buffer
panels.description: Events dropped from the kernel ring buffer per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute), by syscall category (exit events: clone_fork, execve, connect, open, dir_file, close, proc, other_interest). A sign the node produces more events than Falco consumes. Falco 0.45 exports only these exit categories: drops of the open and connect enter events (TOCTOU mitigation) are counted in Scap Drops total but not shown here, and the exported dir="enter" series are fixed zeros. A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Scap Drops Auxmap Pool Full
panels.description: Modern eBPF auxiliary-map pool exhaustion drops per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute). Uses the native metric exported by the installed driver; the legacy CPU-drop metric is not available. A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Scap Drops Full Threadtable
panels.description: Threads Falco could not add to its thread table because it was full, per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute). Events from those threads are still processed but lack process and container context, so rules can misfire or miss. Usually caused by a very large number of live threads; see thread_table_size. A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Scap Drops Scratch Map
panels.description: Events dropped because they exceeded the modern eBPF scratch-map (maximum event size) per displayed interval (minimum 1 minute). A new Falco pod counts every drop since its process started, including drops before its first scrape. A bar equal to a pod's whole running total can appear when the selected range starts before the stored data (14-day retention) or when the scrape labels change without a Falco restart; check the pod's counter before treating it as new drops.

panels.title: Versions
panels.description: Falco versions of the pods reporting at the end of the selected range (current state, not every version seen in the range).

panels.title: Engines
panels.description: Scap engines of the pods reporting at the end of the selected range (current state, not every engine seen in the range). Should be modern_bpf.
